subject: Medicore request: EU-only routing + no-fallback for prod
messages:
From: Patrick Brown <patrick.brown@medicore.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Medicore Security <security@medicore.com>, Medicore Procurement <procurement@medicore.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: EU-only routing + no-fallback for Medicore prod

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Medicore is ready to move a small but critical workload to Redwood for our patient-facing summaries. Before we proceed to procurement, our security/legal teams require two firm controls at the platform level: 1) all production inference for this workload must be routed to EU-only hosts (data residency), and 2) absolutely no fallback to other regions or model variants in prod (no-fallback).

We understand this is a stricter constraint than your default routing/fallback policy; Medicore says this is non-negotiable for regulatory compliance in our EU subsidiaries. We can start with a single model variant and are willing to sign an SLA carve-out if needed. Timeline: target prod cutover week of Nov 15.

Attached: SOC2_questionnaire_v3.pdf (security team) and a short compliance note. Can Redwood confirm operational feasibility and a plan (including capacity reservation and rollback procedures)? Also please advise if there are any product limitations we should surface to our legal team.

—Patrick
Patrick Brown
Head of Integrations, Medicore Health
patrick.brown@medicore.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: EU-only routing + no-fallback for Medicore prod

Patrick — thanks for the clear ask and the SOC2 doc. Looping in Product (Lauren), Ops (Jonas) and Enterprise (Marissa) to triage.

Initial questions from my side:
- Is the EU-only requirement EU region (single region) or EU multi-region within EU (we can pin to eu-west-1 or to any EU footprint)?
- When you say no-fallback, do you mean no automatic fallback under any capacity constraints (i.e., hard-block redirects to other regions) or simply an operational policy that requires approval?
- Do you need forced model selection (single exact model checkpoint) or is a compatible, functionally equivalent variant acceptable?

I attached a short mapping worksheet (prelim-mapping.xlsx) to capture service boundaries. Proposed next step: 30-min triage call tomorrow to align requirements and expected timeline (I can book).

Karthik
Director, Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Patrick Brown <patrick.brown@medicore.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: EU-only routing + no-fallback for Medicore prod

Thanks for looping me in. High-level product notes so the team and Medicore can evaluate trade-offs:

1) EU-only routing: we can support a region lock at the routing layer (route requests to instances in EU-only pools). That is a supported config for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted customers we can create a region-isolated serving pool linked to the account, but it requires capacity reservation on our side.

2) No-fallback (hard): Our standard runtime supports fallback to compatible model variants/regions when an instance is unavailable — this preserves availability. Enforcing a hard no-fallback behavior is possible but has implications:
   - If a node/pool is unavailable, requests will fail instead of routing to a fallback. That will increase error rates unless capacity is overprovisioned.
   - We will need a platform-side flag (hard_region_lock + no_fallback) that disables automatic fallback and disables certain automatic retry/fallback circuitry.

3) Forced model selection: pinning to a single checkpoint is straightforward (pin model id + version). But this removes automatic roll-forward and some safety fallbacks.

Proposed mitigations:
- For production: provision dedicated capacity in EU with a minimum reserve to meet your SLA and enable hard_region_lock + no_fallback.
- For safety: allow a staging canary (same config but in a separate isolated namespace) to exercise failover behavior in a controlled way.

Questions for Medicore: target p95 latency SLO and acceptable error budget if we keep no-fallback? That will drive the reserve size.

I can draft a short change request template (product + ops runbook) if we decide to proceed.

—Lauren
VP, Product — Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Patrick Brown <patrick.brown@medicore.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: EU-only routing + no-fallback for Medicore prod

I ran a quick capacity/ops estimate based on Medicore's approximate volume (from the mapping). Key points:

- To hit a conservative p95 <300ms with no-fallback in EU-only, we should reserve a 35% headroom above steady-state traffic to cover node churn and maintenance windows.
- Capacity reservation approach: we can carve out a dedicated pool (reserved instances) in eu-west-1. This avoids cross-region routing entirely.
- Cost and lead time: reserving this pool for Nov 15 cutover requires approval this week. Estimated monthly incremental cost: ~€18k–€25k depending on model size/quantization. See attached capacity-estimate.csv.

Operational changes required:
- Platform flag: hard_region_lock + no_fallback (ops + runtime change). I can take the lead on a scoped runtime toggle but will need Product to sign off on the behavior (Lauren) and Security to OK the auditability requirements.
- Runbook: emergency rollback will be to disable the mapped route for the Medicore tenant (resulting in 503s) and redirect clients to a maintenance page. We must pre-authorize this in the procurement/SLA.

Action items:
1) Marissa — can you confirm commercial path for capacity reservation + SLA carve-out?
2) Lauren — draft product change + opt-in toggle language for the portal and API.
3) Karthik — schedule triage with Medicore security/legal tomorrow.

Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: EU-only routing + no-fallback for Medicore prod

Patrick — thanks, team. Quick summary and immediate next steps so Medicore has clarity: 

Summary: Redwood can support EU-only routing with a hard no-fallback mode for production by provisioning a reserved dedicated pool in EU and enabling a runtime flag (hard_region_lock + no_fallback). This will require a commercial capacity reservation and an SLA carve-out to cover availability expectations. We will also pin the model checkpoint per your request.

Next steps (this week):
- Jonas to share capacity estimates (done, attached).
- Marissa to confirm commercial terms and a one-off SLA addendum by EOD Tue.
- Lauren to draft the product change request and the portal UI/opt-in language.
- Karthik will schedule a 30-min triage with Medicore security/legal — calendar invite: https://calendar.redwood.com/event/abc123

Patrick, can you confirm: (1) single EU region ok (we recommend eu-west-1), (2) target p95 and any hard cutover blackout windows. If we get confirmation, we can target Nov 15 for prod cutover but we need procurement signed and payment for reserved capacity first.

Thanks — will follow up with the triage invite.

Karthik
Director, Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
